## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

The *Yavapālakavimānavatthu* ("Barley-Warden’s Mansion", Vv 71) is a short Pali verse narrative in the *Vimānavatthu* collection of the Khuddaka Nikāya [SuttaCentral]. In this text, a celestial being who in his past human life worked as a guard protecting a barley field explains the meritorious deeds that led to his rebirth as a *deva* enjoying a heavenly mansion (*vimāna*) [SuttaCentral]. SuttaCentral records four translations of the text across four languages [SuttaCentral].
No direct external parallels are recorded on SuttaCentral, and DharmaNexus reports no cross-language alignments with Chinese, Sanskrit, or Tibetan corpora with a score of 10 or above [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. However, computational analysis by DharmaNexus identifies substantial Pali-internal text reuse, showing 107 matching passages shared with twelve other Pali texts [DharmaNexus]. The largest share of overlap occurs with the text's traditional commentary, the *Vimānavatthu-aṭṭhakathā* (48 matches), alongside formulaic verse parallels shared with other poems within the *Vimānavatthu*, notably the *Guttilavimānavatthu* (Vv 33), *Caturitthivimānavatthu* (Vv 45), *Dutiyabhikkhādāyikāvimānavatthu* (Vv 28), and *Paṭhamabhikkhādāyikāvimānavatthu* (Vv 27) [DharmaNexus].
